angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: brake into the cut, speed through it, drive out), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families (slant/out/hitch/in/corner), tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out draft classes; positive use: last season's route-shrunk SOE as a tiebreaker for day-3 and undrafted receivers.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills.
headline_number: Primary (pre-specified offset forecast): -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [-3.6, +1.0], n=116 on unseen classes; +3 in rejected (p=0.001) in every one of 8 variants (largest p 0.006). Day-3/UDFA tiebreaker: rank correlation 0.37 vs 0.06 for pick and routes (gain +0.31 [-0.08, +0.63], within-fold shuffle p=0.01); yes/no list 7/13 vs 6/13 (shuffle p=0.11).
what_changed_from_previous: Revision of the round-14 winner. Football: one-verdict headline table that holds the rank correlation, its interval, the shuffle p and the yes/no count (abstract no longer quotes conflicting numbers); SOE framed as a tiebreaker only; worked roster decision (Demario Douglas vs Ryan Flournoy: same pick and routes, 57% vs 56% from pick and routes, 91% vs 32% with SOE, 15.6 in forecast gap = 2.3 catches a season at the same ~$1M cap cost); 2026 Combine protocol (double-rep slant, dagger, comeback; use the official 40 because the tracked clip starts ~0.3 s early); team, alignment and games columns on the 2026 list; new finding that, given pick, hard cutters are likelier to reach 100 routes (OR 2.09 [1.10, 4.52]) without separating more. Ridge/QB rows moved to the appendix. Data science: selection model and IPW primary (-0.8 [-2.8, +1.3]; 33 of 149 excluded, reported); receiver random-intercept mixed models (season SOE slope -0.5 [-2.8, +1.8]; persistence 0.63 [0.17, 1.09]); permutation tests of the 7/13 vs 6/13 gap (p=0.11) and of the rank-correlation gain (p=0.01); calibration by bin and slope (1.19 [0.47, 1.91]; level runs ~10 points high on day 3, stated); one appendix table of slopes across plain, ridge, no-offset, IPW, mixed, no-Nacua, route-mix and QB with a single one-sided test at +3 in. numbers.json is filtered automatically to numbers quoted in the text. Writeup: short title (the judge's suggestion), 3-sentence lede, 'Why it matters' rewritten as the roster decision, one-sentence metric, named-cases paragraph and drill/tape table cut, hedges collapsed into one verdict line; 1,991 words, 4 figures and 3 tables. Viz: Fig 1 shared 2-yd scale bar, 10.5 pt readouts, regression-to-the-mean footnote; Fig 2C greys slices with NFL reliability below 0.10; Fig 3 prints each price and value (Break G price 9% in the figure and the text); Fig 4 sorted by outcome with tick/cross hit marks, larger panel B and a new calibration panel C.
open_risks: Headline is a bounded null: gains above +1.0 in per sd are excluded, losses down to -3.6 are not

Day-3 edge: the shuffle test says last season's SOE carries signal (p=0.01), but the clustered interval for the size of the gain includes zero and it wins 1 of 2 folds; the yes/no list gap is not significant (p=0.11)
Held-out probabilities rank well but run about 10 points high on day 3 (50% forecast vs 40% observed); the 2026 list probabilities are not recalibrated
The worked case was chosen by a stated rule (largest SOE-forecast gap among pick- and route-matched 2025 day-3 WR pairs), so it is the most favourable illustration, not a typical one
Games played is a rough injury proxy; scheme context is limited to team and main alignment
Game tracking is a 40-play sample per player, half selected for high EPA; earlier rounds saw all three classes, so the 2026 class is the first blind test
